nodes.label: PKCε (epsilon isoform)
nodes.rationale: PKCε is the primary nociceptor isoform; it phosphorylates TRPV1 (Ser800), Nav1.8, Nav1.7, TRPA1, and KCC2 (Thr906/Thr1007), making it the master regulator of peripheral sensitisation. Genetic deletion (Prkce-/-) markedly reduces allodynia.

nodes.label: PKCγ (gamma isoform)
nodes.rationale: PKCγ is selectively expressed in spinal lamina IIi excitatory interneurons. After nerve injury disinhibition allows Aβ fibres to activate PKCγ+ neurons, driving mechanical allodynia. Prkcc-/- mice are protected from tactile allodynia.

nodes.label: PKC-dependent KCC2 phosphorylation at Thr906/Thr1007
nodes.rationale: PKCε and PKCγ phosphorylate KCC2 at Thr906 and Thr1007, promoting endocytosis, lysosomal degradation, and disinhibition independently of BDNF-TrkB signaling.

nodes.label: Smad2 (TGF-β downstream)
nodes.rationale: Smad2 activation mediates the anti-nociceptive, anti-inflammatory, and KCC2-promoting effects of TGF-β. Selectively enhancing Smad2 while inhibiting Smad3 is the proposed therapeutic strategy.

nodes.label: Smad3 (TGF-β downstream)
nodes.rationale: Smad3 is the primary driver of perineural fibrosis, astroglial scar formation, and cellular senescence (SASP) that perpetuate chronic pain. SIS3 (Smad3-selective inhibitor) reduces fibrosis and allodynia.

nodes.label: ALK5 (TGF-β receptor type I)
nodes.rationale: ALK5 is the primary small-molecule target for TGF-β pathway inhibition. Early ALK5 inhibition worsens pain; delayed inhibition in the chronic phase reduces fibrosis.

nodes.label: HMGB1 (High Mobility Group Box 1)
nodes.rationale: HMGB1 is the primary endogenous DAMP released after nerve injury that activates TLR4 on microglia, neurons, and astrocytes, initiating the neuroinflammatory cascade.

nodes.label: MyD88 (TLR4 adaptor protein)
nodes.rationale: MyD88-dependent TLR4 signaling leads to NF-κB activation and pro-inflammatory cytokine transcription, essential for the initiation of neuropathic pain.

nodes.label: TRIF (TLR4 adaptor protein)
nodes.rationale: TRIF-dependent TLR4 pathway activates IRF3 and late-phase NF-κB, contributing to sustained neuroinflammation.

nodes.label: TLR4-ferroptosis axis
nodes.rationale: TLR4 signaling upregulates HO-1, releases free iron, promotes lipid peroxidation and ferroptotic cell death, releasing additional DAMPs in a feed-forward loop.

nodes.label: PV+ GABAergic interneuron apoptosis
nodes.rationale: Selective apoptosis of parvalbumin-positive fast-spiking GABAergic interneurons by caspase-3 is the primary mechanism linking calcium overload to mechanical allodynia via structural disinhibition.

nodes.label: Non-apoptotic caspase-3 functions
nodes.rationale: Caspase-3 cleaves PKCδ (generates constitutively active fragment promoting microglial activation) and AMPA receptor GluA1 (facilitating maladaptive LTD). These non-death functions amplify neuroinflammation and maladaptive plasticity.

nodes.label: MEK1/2 (MAP2K upstream of ERK)
nodes.rationale: MEK1/2 are the direct kinases phosphorylating ERK1/2. MEK inhibitors (trametinib, U0126) are the primary pharmacological tool to validate ERK's role in pain and are FDA-approved for oncology with repurposing potential.

nodes.label: CREB transcription factor (ERK downstream)
nodes.rationale: ERK-phosphorylated CREB at Ser133 drives transcription of BDNF, COX-2, prodynorphin, NK1R, and c-fos, consolidating central sensitisation as a transcriptional memory.

nodes.label: MMP-9 (Matrix Metalloproteinase-9)
nodes.rationale: MMP-9 is the executioner of PNN degradation after nerve injury. It cleaves aggrecan, dismantles the PNN lattice around PV interneurons (reducing fast-spiking capacity), and converts pro-BDNF to mature BDNF, simultaneously enabling structural and ionic disinhibition.

nodes.label: Chondroitin Sulfate Proteoglycans (CSPGs)
nodes.rationale: CSPGs (aggrecan, versican, neurocan, brevican) are the major structural PNN components. Their degradation is the primary mechanism of PNN breakdown; aggrecan-NITEGE fragments serve as specific biomarkers of PNN attrition.

nodes.label: Ceftriaxone (GLT-1 upregulator)
nodes.rationale: Ceftriaxone is the prototype GLT-1 upregulator acting via Slc1a2 promoter activation, independent of its antibiotic activity. Analgesic efficacy is abolished by GLT-1 inhibitor DHK or antisense knockdown, confirming GLT-1 specificity.

nodes.label: Glutamate spillover in dorsal horn
nodes.rationale: GLT-1 downregulation causes 2-3 fold increase in extracellular glutamate, tonically activating extrasynaptic GluN2B NMDARs, driving Ca2+ overload, caspase-3 activation, and GABAergic interneuron apoptosis. This is the primary upstream event of structural disinhibition.

nodes.label: COX-2 (Cyclooxygenase-2)
nodes.rationale: COX-2 is dramatically upregulated at the nerve injury site and in spinal endothelial cells. COX-2-derived PGE2 via EP4 receptor drives de novo IL-6 synthesis in DRG neurons, coupling prostaglandin signaling to cytokine cascades.

nodes.label: EP4 receptor (PGE2 receptor)
nodes.rationale: EP4 is the most abundant PGE2 receptor in injured nerve. EP4 activation drives de novo IL-6 synthesis via PKA/PKC/ERK/CREB/NF-κB, anterograde trafficking of EP4 to nociceptor terminals, and prolonged sensitization.

nodes.label: Prostaglandin D2 (PGD2)
nodes.rationale: PGD2 is the most abundant CNS prostanoid. COX-1-dependent microglial PGD2 acts via DP2 receptors on spinal neurons as a key microglia-to-neuron pain signal for mechanical allodynia.

nodes.label: CSF1R (receptor tyrosine kinase)
nodes.rationale: CSF1R on spinal microglia mediates CSF1-driven proliferation and activation. Downstream DAP12 signaling controls pain-related gene expression independently of proliferation; p38 MAPK drives BDNF release and KCC2 downregulation.

nodes.label: IL-34 (alternative CSF1R ligand)
nodes.rationale: IL-34 from Schwann cells in the DRG is a second CSF1R ligand mediating Schwann cell-macrophage crosstalk after nerve injury. Paeonol and stigmasterol inhibit the IL-34/CSF1R interaction.

nodes.label: NICD (Notch Intracellular Domain)
nodes.rationale: NICD is released by γ-secretase cleavage and translocates to the nucleus to activate Hes/Hey target genes. NICD-NF-κB complex amplifies TNF-α and IL-1β transcription, forming a feed-forward inflammatory loop.

nodes.label: DAPT (γ-secretase inhibitor)
nodes.rationale: DAPT is the prototype Notch pathway inhibitor. Intrathecal DAPT reduces allodynia, microglial/astrocytic activation, NICD/Hes1 expression, and downregulates Nav1.7/Nav1.8/TRPV1 without affecting naïve pain thresholds.

nodes.label: HIF1α (master transcriptional hub)
nodes.rationale: HIF1α undergoes normoxic stabilization by ROS and TNF-α after nerve injury, driving VEGFA/ANGPT2 upregulation (leaky vasculature), MMP-9 activation (PNN/ECM degradation), and metabolic reprogramming (Warburg shift in microglia). It is the primary upstream master switch of the neuropathic state.

nodes.label: God Node / Network Hub Concept
nodes.rationale: The roadmap proposes targeting high-traffic master regulators (God Nodes) that govern interconnected vascular, metabolic, and structural pathways instead of single-molecule inhibition, to achieve disease modification rather than symptom management.

nodes.label: AMG487 (CXCR3 antagonist)
nodes.rationale: AMG487 is an orally bioavailable allosteric CXCR3 antagonist that reverses mechanical allodynia, reduces Iba-1+ microglia, suppresses TNF-α/IL-1β/BDNF, and partially restores KCC2 in CCI models. Analgesic effects absent in Cxcr3-/- mice.

nodes.label: IL-6 trans-signaling via sIL-6R/gp130
nodes.rationale: IL-6 trans-signaling (IL-6 + soluble IL-6R forming hyperIL-6, activating gp130 on cells lacking membrane IL-6R) is the dominant pathogenic mechanism enabling IL-6 to directly excite nociceptors and activate spinal glia. sgp130Fc (olamkicept) selectively blocks trans-signaling while preserving classical signaling.

nodes.label: JAK/STAT3 pathway (IL-6 downstream)
nodes.rationale: JAK1/JAK2 activation by gp130 phosphorylates STAT3 (Tyr705), which drives autocrine IL-6 loops, SOCS3 negative feedback, and transcription of pronociceptive effectors including TNF-α, IL-1β, CCL2, COX-2, BDNF, VEGF, MMP-9.

nodes.label: β-catenin (canonical Wnt mediator)
nodes.rationale: β-catenin/TCF transcription drives IL-18, TNF-α, MMP-9, and α2δ-1 calcium channel subunit expression in spinal glia and neurons. β-catenin conditional knockout in sensory neurons reduces allodynia and MMP-9 levels.

nodes.label: Wnt5a/Ryk non-canonical Ca2+ pathway
nodes.rationale: Wnt5a binding to Ryk or Fzd activates PLC, generating IP3/DAG, releasing intracellular Ca2+, and activating PKC/Src to phosphorylate GluN2B, enhancing NMDAR conductance and driving central sensitization rapidly.

nodes.label: Resolvin D1 (RvD1)
nodes.rationale: RvD1 acts via ALX/FPR2 on spinal microglia and neurons to reverse allodynia, restore blood-nerve barrier tight junctions (suppressing MMP-9), shift microglia M1→M2, and synergize with low-dose morphine. Equally effective in male and female rodents, unlike microglial-targeted inhibitors.

nodes.label: Maresin 1 (MaR1)
nodes.rationale: MaR1 is the most potent SPM for pain (ED50 ~1 ng i.t.). Acts via LGR6 on astrocytes and microglia. Promotes efferocytosis and myelin debris clearance (addressing Nogo-A/NgR1 pathway). Restores corneal nerve fiber density in diabetic neuropathy.

nodes.label: Lipoxin A4 (LXA4)
nodes.rationale: LXA4 acts via ALX/FPR2 (shared with RvD1) and PPARγ to reduce allodynia, inhibit neutrophil infiltration into DRG/spinal cord, suppress MMP-9, and activate resolution programs. Endogenous LXA4 biosynthesis is suppressed in neuropathic pain.

nodes.label: CLP257/CLP290 (KCC2 enhancers)
nodes.rationale: CLP257 and its prodrug CLP290 directly enhance KCC2 activity by stabilizing surface expression. CLP290 is orally bioavailable and in Phase I/II trials for spinal cord injury spasticity. Analgesic effects confirmed in SNI, nerve injury, and spinal cord injury pain models.

nodes.label: BDNF-TrkB-KCC2 disinhibition cascade
nodes.rationale: Microglial-derived BDNF binds TrkB on lamina I neurons, activating Src (phosphorylates KCC2 Tyr1087) and PLCγ-PKC (phosphorylates Thr906/Thr1007), causing KCC2 endocytosis and degradation. This is the canonical disinhibition mechanism of mechanical allodynia.

nodes.label: ARN23746 (next-gen KCC2 activator)
nodes.rationale: ARN23746 (2024) shows 50-fold improved potency (EC50 ~50 nM vs ~2.5 µM for CLP257), >100-fold selectivity over NKCC1. Structure-guided optimization from cryo-EM KCC2 structures. Reverses allodynia at 1 mg/kg i.p. in SNI mice.

nodes.label: WNK-SPAK pathway (KCC2 regulation)
nodes.rationale: WNK kinases phosphorylate SPAK/OSR1, which activate NKCC1 and inhibit KCC2. WNK463 and closantel simultaneously reduce NKCC1 and enhance KCC2 activity, restoring the chloride gradient. This pathway is hyperactivated after nerve injury.

nodes.label: Neuronal CCL2 release from injured primary afferents
nodes.rationale: CCL2 released from central terminals of injured primary afferents binds CCR2 on spinal microglia, triggering BDNF/TNF-α/IL-1β release. CCL2 also directly depolarizes DRG neurons and enhances TRPV1/Nav1.8/HCN2 activity via CCR2.
nodes.norm_label: neuronal ccl2 release from injured primary afferents

nodes.label: IRF8 (P2X4 transcriptional regulator)
nodes.rationale: IRF8 is a master regulator of pro-inflammatory microglial phenotype that directly drives P2rx4 transcription after nerve injury. IRF8 knockout mice fail to upregulate P2X4 and are protected from allodynia.

nodes.label: Fibronectin-integrin β1 priming of P2X4
nodes.rationale: Fibronectin accumulating in spinal dorsal horn after injury binds integrin β1 on microglia, signaling through PI3K to open and stably upregulate P2X4 channels, priming them for enhanced ATP responsiveness.

nodes.label: LY2828360 (G-protein biased CB2 agonist)
nodes.rationale: LY2828360 is a slowly-signaling, G-protein-biased CB2 agonist that suppresses paclitaxel-induced neuropathic pain without tolerance, prolongs opioid analgesia, and reduces opioid dependence. Failed in osteoarthritis clinical trial, suggesting pain-type specificity.

nodes.label: β-Caryophyllene (natural CB2 agonist)
nodes.rationale: β-Caryophyllene is a dietary sesquiterpene (in black pepper, cloves) that is a selective full CB2 agonist. Oral BCP alleviates allodynia, reduces TNF-α/IL-1β/IL-6, and attenuates oxidative stress in diabetic neuropathy models with excellent safety profile.

nodes.label: Meningeal ILC2-GM-CSF-vertebral myelopoiesis axis
nodes.rationale: A 2025 landmark finding: meningeal ILC2s surrounding DRG are the primary source of GM-CSF after nerve injury. GM-CSF diffuses via CSF to vertebral bone marrow, driving emergency myelopoiesis. Newly generated neutrophils and monocytes migrate to DRG meninges and promote pain chronicity. This defines neuropathic pain partly as a vertebral bone marrow-driven neuroinflammation disorder.

nodes.label: Otilimab (anti-GM-CSF mAb)
nodes.rationale: Otilimab (GSK3196165) is a human anti-GM-CSF mAb in Phase III trials for RA (contRAst program). Produces rapid, significant analgesic effects in RA dissociable from anti-inflammatory effects, validating GM-CSF as a human pain mediator.

nodes.label: Suzetrigine/VX-548 (Nav1.8 inhibitor, FDA-approved 2025)
nodes.rationale: Suzetrigine (VX-548) is the first FDA-approved (2025) Nav1.8-selective inhibitor for acute pain. State-independent mechanism. Phase II/III trials for neuropathic pain ongoing. Represents the first clinical validation of Nav1.8 as an analgesic target.

nodes.label: ANP-230 (multi-Nav blocker Nav1.7/1.8/1.9)
nodes.rationale: ANP-230 is a peripherally-restricted, state-independent blocker of Nav1.7, Nav1.8, and Nav1.9. Shows superior efficacy vs pregabalin in multiple preclinical pain models with negligible motor impairment. Potentiates morphine analgesia. Addresses functional redundancy among Nav isoforms.

nodes.label: SCN9A loss-of-function (congenital indifference to pain)
nodes.rationale: Loss-of-function mutations in SCN9A cause congenital indifference to pain with anosmia but no other neurological deficits, providing the original human genetic rationale for Nav1.7 as an analgesic target.

nodes.label: TrkB.FL (Full-Length TrkB Receptor)
nodes.rationale: TrkB.FL on lamina I projection neurons mediates pronociceptive BDNF signaling: KCC2 downregulation, GluN2B phosphorylation, LTP at C-fiber synapses. The primary kinase target for neuropathic pain.

nodes.label: TrkB.T1 (Truncated Isoform)
nodes.rationale: TrkB.T1 lacks the kinase domain but has active signaling; it is the predominant TrkB isoform in nociceptors and upregulated after injury. ANA-12 also blocks TrkB.T1, adding complexity to TrkB targeting.

nodes.label: proBDNF / p75NTR Signaling
nodes.rationale: proBDNF binds p75NTR promoting apoptosis. MMP-9 cleaves proBDNF to mBDNF, shifting the balance toward pronociceptive TrkB.FL signaling. Inhibiting MMP-9 reduces mBDNF and allodynia.

nodes.label: BDNF Val66Met Polymorphism
nodes.rationale: Val66Met reduces activity-dependent BDNF secretion. Complex effects on pain: protective in some conditions, harmful in others depending on etiology and sex. Important human genetic variable for precision analgesia.

nodes.label: TrkB-Fc (BDNF Sequestering Chimera)
nodes.rationale: TrkB-Fc scavenges BDNF intrathecally and consistently reduces mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia in CCI and SNL models. Gold-standard tool for BDNF pathway validation.

nodes.label: TNFR1 (TNF Receptor 1, pronociceptive)
nodes.rationale: TNFR1 binds soluble TNF-α and initiates NF-κB/MAPK inflammatory signaling that drives neuronal sensitization and microglial activation. XPro1595 selectively blocks solTNF/TNFR1 without impairing tmTNF/TNFR2 neuroprotection.

nodes.label: TNFR2 (TNF Receptor 2, neuroprotective)
nodes.rationale: TNFR2 activation promotes pain resolution: M1→M2 microglial shift, lipoxin/RvD1 induction, neuroprotection. TNFR2-selective agonism provides long-lasting pain resolution and is the therapeutic complement to TNFR1 blockade.

nodes.label: XPro1595 (TNFR1-Selective solTNF Blocker)
nodes.rationale: XPro1595 is a dominant-negative TNF that selectively neutralizes solTNF/TNFR1 signaling while preserving tmTNF/TNFR2. Reduces peripheral neuropathies and microglial activation without pan-TNF suppression risks.

nodes.label: ANA-12 Non-Competitive TrkB Binding
nodes.rationale: ANA-12 binds the specificity interaction patch of TrkB (IC50=45.6 nM), preventing BDNF-mediated signaling without affecting TrkA or TrkC. Brain-penetrant at 0.5 mg/kg i.p. Suppresses spinal TNF-α, IL-1β, NF-κB, and NLRP3 component expression.

nodes.label: ANA-12 KCC2 Preservation via TrkB Blockade
nodes.rationale: ANA-12 opposes BDNF-driven KCC2 downregulation and NMDA receptor potentiation at GluN2B, restoring inhibitory tone. Validates TrkB-KCC2 axis as sequential therapeutic target.
nodes.norm_label: ana-12 kcc2 preservation via trkb blockade

nodes.label: CP-AMPARs (GluA2-lacking) in PV Neurons
nodes.rationale: PV interneurons express high levels of GluA2-lacking Ca2+-permeable AMPARs. Sustained glutamatergic drive causes massive Ca2+ entry, triggering mitochondrial damage and apoptosis. IEM-1460 blocks CP-AMPARs and protects PV neurons.

nodes.label: mPTP Opening / Mitochondrial Failure
nodes.rationale: Excessive mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake opens mPTP, collapses ATP production, generates ROS burst releasing cytochrome c. Cyclosporin A/NIM811 inhibit cyclophilin D-dependent mPTP opening and reduce allodynia.

nodes.label: Calpain-Mediated Cleavage (Ca2+-Activated)
nodes.rationale: Sustained Ca2+ activates calpain which cleaves ATG5, Beclin-1 (impairing autophagy), and KCC2 C-terminus. MDL-28170 calpain inhibitor preserves GABAergic neurons and reduces pain behaviors.

nodes.label: Rapamycin / mTOR Inhibition (Autophagy Restoration)
nodes.rationale: mTORC1 hyperactivation by Ca2+ influx blocks autophagy initiation. Rapamycin/rapalogs restore autophagic flux, clear damaged mitochondria, protect GABAergic neurons from apoptosis, and reduce mechanical allodynia.

nodes.label: Ru360 / MCU Blockade
nodes.rationale: The MCU inhibitor Ru360 blocks mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake, prevents mPTP opening, and protects GABAergic neurons from apoptosis, reducing neuropathic pain.

nodes.label: PV Feedforward Inhibition Gate
nodes.rationale: PV interneurons (laminae I-III) gate Aβ-fiber tactile input by feedforward inhibition, preventing touch from activating nociceptive circuits. Their failure is the cellular basis of mechanical allodynia.

nodes.label: PV Inhibition KCC2-Dependency
nodes.rationale: PV interneuron inhibitory output depends on KCC2-maintained low intracellular Cl-. BDNF-TrkB-driven KCC2 downregulation reduces functional inhibition even before PV cell death occurs.

nodes.label: Chemogenetic/Optogenetic PV Rescue
nodes.rationale: DREADD/ChR2 activation of surviving PV interneurons powerfully suppresses mechanical allodynia in nerve-injured animals, proving that boosting residual PV output is sufficient for analgesia.

nodes.label: SST Interneurons as Excitatory Pain Drivers
nodes.rationale: Spinal SST interneurons (lamina II) are glutamatergic. They relay Aβ-fiber touch to lamina I nociceptive neurons. After PV interneuron loss they become disinhibited and drive mechanical allodynia. Ablation or chemogenetic silencing reverses allodynia.
nodes.norm_label: sst interneurons as excitatory pain drivers

nodes.label: Prdm12 Transcription Factor (SST Development)
nodes.rationale: Prdm12 specifies spinal SST interneuron identity. Prdm12-knockout mice lack SST interneurons and show near-complete absence of mechanical allodynia after nerve injury, confirming causal role.

nodes.label: SSTR2a Receptor (SST Autoregulation)
nodes.rationale: SSTR2a is the predominant SST receptor in spinal cord. Its role is complex: SST released after injury acts on SSTR2a but effects can be paradoxically pronociceptive in disinhibition context. SSTR2a antagonists are being explored as analgesics.

nodes.label: ROCK (ROCK1/ROCK2 Kinases)
nodes.rationale: ROCK phosphorylates LIMK→cofilin (actin stabilization), p38 MAPK (microglial M1 activation), and MARCKS (neurotransmitter release amplification). Fasudil (approved for cerebral vasospasm) is the prototype ROCK inhibitor for pain repurposing.

nodes.label: LPA-RhoA-Demyelination Cascade
nodes.rationale: Lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) generated post-injury signals via LPAR1→RhoA/ROCK to demyelinate DRG neurons, causing mechanical allodynia. Blocking this cascade prevents both demyelination and pain.

nodes.label: Fasudil (ROCK Inhibitor, Clinically Approved)
nodes.rationale: Fasudil is approved in Japan for subarachnoid hemorrhage. Attenuates neuropathic pain in CCI/TCI/post-stroke models. Repurposing trials for ALS and Parkinson's provide clinical scaffold for pain trials.

nodes.label: Simvastatin (RhoA Prenylation Inhibitor)
nodes.rationale: Simvastatin depletes mevalonate/geranylgeranyl isoprenoids, preventing RhoA membrane anchoring. Intrathecal simvastatin blocks allodynia and astrogliosis. Explains partial analgesic effects of statins in diabetic neuropathy.

nodes.label: HIF1α Normoxic Stabilization by ROS/TNF/NF-kB
nodes.rationale: After nerve injury, ROS, succinate, NO, and TNF-α inhibit PHD enzymes or activate NF-κB, stabilizing HIF1α under normoxia. This drives a transcriptional program covering VEGFA, ANGPT2, MMP-9, iNOS, BDNF, Nav1.7, Nav1.8, TRPV1.

nodes.label: HIF1α Transcriptional Battery (Pain Genes)
nodes.rationale: HIF1α drives VEGFA, ANGPT2, MMP-2/9, iNOS, COX-2, LDHA/PDK1 (Warburg shift), BDNF (indirectly), Nav1.7, Nav1.8, TRPV1. A master transcriptional hub amplifying all major pain pathways simultaneously.

nodes.label: YC-1 (HIF1α Destabilizer)
nodes.rationale: YC-1 promotes HIF1α degradation. Systemic/intrathecal YC-1 significantly reduces mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia in CCI/SNI models, associated with reduced VEGFA, iNOS, and glycolytic enzymes.

nodes.label: PX-478 (HIF1α Translation Inhibitor)
nodes.rationale: PX-478 inhibits HIF1α translation. Intrathecal PX-478 reduces microglial activation, neuroinflammation, and pain behaviors in CCI. Tested in oncology trials (safety data available), repurposing candidate.

nodes.label: HIF1α-Driven Microglial Glycolytic Shift (M1)
nodes.rationale: HIF1α stabilization in spinal microglia drives Warburg shift (oxidative phosphorylation→glycolysis), M1 pro-inflammatory phenotype, TNF-α/IL-1β/BDNF secretion. 2-DG glycolysis inhibitor reduces microglial activation and allodynia.

nodes.label: Tight Junction Proteins (Occludin, Claudin-5, ZO-1)
nodes.rationale: Occludin, claudin-5, and ZO-1 form the physical BBB/BSCB seal. TNF-α, IL-1β, MMP-9, and VEGFA significantly downregulate these proteins in neuropathic pain states, increasing CNS permeability to circulating pronociceptive mediators.

nodes.label: CypA-MMP-9 Pathway (BBB Degradation)
nodes.rationale: Cyclophilin A (CypA) activates MMP-9 which degrades basement membrane and tight junctions. CsA (cyclosporine A) inhibiting CypA promotes BSCB repair and alleviates neuropathic pain in animal models.

nodes.label: Resolvin D1 / Lipoxin A4 (Barrier Resealing)
nodes.rationale: SPMs (RvD1, LXA4) actively resolve neuroinflammation and reseal the blood-nerve barrier. Represent disease-modifying treatment potential rather than mere symptom management.

nodes.label: P-Glycoprotein Efflux Pump (Drug Delivery Barrier)
nodes.rationale: P-gp is a major efflux transporter modified by pain states, affecting CNS drug accumulation. Its dysregulation in neuropathic pain can have unpredictable effects on analgesic CNS exposure.

nodes.label: Angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2, Vascular Destabilizer)
nodes.rationale: Ang-2 is markedly upregulated in spinal dorsal horn and injured nerves after peripheral nerve injury, driving pathological angiogenesis, BSCB disruption, macrophage activation, and TNF-α/IL-1β release. Potential serum/CSF biomarker for pain severity.

nodes.label: Tie2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinase
nodes.rationale: Tie2 is expressed on endothelial cells, pericytes, neurons, and immune cells. Ang-1 activates Tie2 (vascular stability); Ang-2 acts as a functional antagonist in inflammation. Constitutively activating Tie2 mutations cause painful venous malformations.

nodes.label: COMP-Ang-1 (Stabilized Ang-1 Therapeutic)
nodes.rationale: COMP-Ang-1 (cartilage oligomeric matrix protein-Ang-1) reduces pro-inflammatory markers, improves nerve conduction, and promotes microvascular regeneration in diabetic ob/ob mice. Clinical repurposing candidate for vascular neuropathic pain.

nodes.label: VEGFR2 (Pronociceptive VEGFA Receptor)
nodes.rationale: VEGFR2 is expressed on DRG neurons, Schwann cells, macrophages, and spinal glia. Activation sensitizes TRPV1/TRPA1/Nav1.8, promotes microglial BDNF release, and disrupts BSCB via tight-junction downregulation.

nodes.label: Neuropilin-1 (NRP-1) Co-Receptor
nodes.rationale: NRP-1 enhances VEGFR2 signaling on nociceptors. Semaphorin-3A antagonizes VEGFA/NRP-1 to block VEGFR2-dependent pain without abolishing neuroprotective VEGFA roles via VEGFR1.

nodes.label: Neuroma Formation via Excessive VEGFA
nodes.rationale: VEGFA drives disorganized angiogenesis at regenerating nerve tips, promoting painful neuroma formation with chronic inflammatory environment and ectopic firing from axonal sprouts.

nodes.label: IGF2 (Insulin-like Growth Factor 2, Pro-nociceptive)
nodes.rationale: IGF2 spinal levels increase significantly after SNI. siRNA knockdown of IGF2 provides 10-day pain relief. NTRK1 upregulation drives IGF2-dependent ER stress to sustain chronic post-surgical pain (2025 study). Key new target.

nodes.label: NTRK1→IGF2→ER Stress Cascade
nodes.rationale: Unidirectional cascade: NTRK1 upregulation drives IGF2-dependent ER stress in spinal cord to sustain chronic post-surgical pain. Inhibiting IGF2 alleviates both ER stress and pain. Novel target distinct from BDNF/TrkB axis.

nodes.label: IGF2BP2 (m6A Reader Stabilizing Pain Transcripts)
nodes.rationale: Histone lactylation in injured DRG drives IGF2BP2 expression, an m6A mRNA reader that stabilizes pro-nociceptive transcripts. Connects IGF signaling network to epigenetic pain mechanisms.

nodes.label: NrCAM Exon 10 Retention (Rbfox1 Loss Effect)
nodes.rationale: Rbfox1 downregulation in injured DRG causes exon 10 retention in NrCAM mRNA, increasing long L-NrCAM isoform. ASO targeting L-NrCAM partially reverses SNL-induced allodynia within 72h. Validates splice-switching as analgesic strategy.

nodes.label: Rbfox1-SCN9A mRNA Stability (Nav1.7 Regulation)
nodes.rationale: Rbfox1 regulates SCN9A (Nav1.7) mRNA stability via PABPC1 and m6A methylation. Rbfox1 loss increases Nav1.7 expression, providing a second route for DRG hyperexcitability independent of NrCAM splicing.

nodes.label: AAV5-Rbfox1 Gene Therapy (Pain Prevention)
nodes.rationale: AAV5-Rbfox1 delivery to DRG before SNL preserves Rbfox1 levels and significantly attenuates mechanical allodynia, thermal hyperalgesia, and spinal central sensitization. Proof-of-concept for splicing-master gene therapy.

nodes.label: NgR1 (Nogo-66 Receptor 1)
nodes.rationale: NgR1 (GPI-anchored) forms tripartite complex with LINGO-1 and p75NTR/TROY, converging signals from Nogo-A, MAG, and OMgp onto RhoA/ROCK activation. Genetic NgR1 knockout shows reduced pain sensitivity and enhanced nerve injury recovery.

nodes.label: Nogo-A/NgR1 TRPV1 Membrane Stabilization
nodes.rationale: Nogo-A binds NgR1, activating LIMK/cofilin-dependent actin polymerization that stabilizes TRPV1 on plasma membrane, promoting inflammatory heat hyperalgesia. Anti-Nogo-A antibodies reduce TRPV1 membrane content and alleviate heat hyperalgesia.

nodes.label: NG101 (Anti-Nogo-A Antibody, NISCI Trial)
nodes.rationale: NG101 (Phase II multicenter NISCI trial) improved neurological recovery in acute SCI patients. Pain outcomes (secondary endpoint) are being analyzed. Opens clinical pathway for anti-Nogo-A therapy in neuropathic pain.

nodes.label: LINGO-1 (NgR1 Co-Receptor, Remyelination Target)
nodes.rationale: LINGO-1 is essential for NgR1 complex function and inhibits remyelination. Anti-LINGO-1 antibodies (opicinumab, Phase II MS trials) block myelin-inhibitor signaling and promote remyelination, potential analgesic in demyelinating pain.

nodes.label: IL-6/gp130/JAK2 Axis
nodes.rationale: IL-6 binding to gp130 activates JAK2→STAT3(Tyr705). Activated STAT3 drives reactive glial transcriptome: IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6 autocrine loop, CCL2, BDNF, COX-2, iNOS, MMP-9, NLRP3 upregulation. Master sustainer of chronic neuroinflammation.

nodes.label: SOCS3 (Negative Regulator of JAK/STAT3)
nodes.rationale: SOCS3 is induced by STAT3 itself to terminate signaling (negative feedback). In chronic pain, SOCS3 is downregulated or insufficient, enabling sustained STAT3 activity. AAV-mediated SOCS3 overexpression reduces neuropathic pain in CCI/SNL models.

nodes.label: Ruxolitinib (JAK1/2 Inhibitor, FDA-Approved)
nodes.rationale: Ruxolitinib is approved for myelofibrosis. Attenuates mechanical allodynia, reduces glial activation, and normalizes STAT3-dependent gene expression in preclinical pain models. Repurposing candidate for neuropathic pain.

nodes.label: Baricitinib (JAK1/2 Inhibitor, RA-Approved)
nodes.rationale: Baricitinib is approved for RA. Clinical trial for chronic low back pain is ongoing. JAK inhibitor repurposing for neuropathic pain is the fastest-to-clinic strategy, leveraging existing safety profiles.

nodes.label: NMDAR (GluN2B/GluN2A) as Plasticity Marker
nodes.rationale: GluN2B:GluN2A ratio at synapses determines LTP/LTD threshold. GluN2B-rich synapses have lower plasticity threshold. BDNF-TrkB signaling potentiates NMDAR via GluN2B phosphorylation, driving pain LTP.

nodes.label: PSD-95 (Postsynaptic Density Scaffolding)
nodes.rationale: PSD-95 clusters and anchors glutamate receptors at excitatory synapses. Its disruption reflects synaptic structural remodeling. Loss of PSD-95 after TBI coincides with dendritic spine loss.

nodes.label: CaMKII (LTP Kinase, Structural Plasticity)
nodes.rationale: CaMKII activated by NMDAR Ca2+ influx autophosphorylates and inserts GluA1-AMPARs, driving spine growth and LTP. Essential for pain-related synaptic plasticity consolidation.

nodes.label: In Vivo Multimodal Circuit Dissection Skill
nodes.norm_label: in vivo multimodal circuit dissection skill

nodes.label: Closed-Loop Neuromodulation for Pain
nodes.rationale: Adaptive optogenetic/chemogenetic/electrical stimulation triggered by real-time neural/behavioral thresholds. State-gated therapy avoids motor/cognitive side effects of tonic stimulation. Key innovation for PV interneuron rescue strategy.

nodes.label: Neuropixels Ensemble Recording (Pain Circuits)
nodes.rationale: High-density electrophysiology across DRG, dorsal horn, thalamus, ACC, PAG enables real-time pain-state decoding. HMM/GLM decoders triggering closed-loop interventions at chronification thresholds.

nodes.label: Cross-Pathway Integrative Therapeutic Appraisals
nodes.rationale: 13 mechanistic dossiers synthesized with god-node framework to generate 13 multi-pathway therapeutic appraisals (HIF1a window destabilization, TNFR1-biased blockade, Rbfox1 splice triad, NTRK1-IGF2-ER stress, closed-loop PV boost+CLP257+IEM-1460, etc.).

nodes.label: KCC2 (Shared Node)
nodes.rationale: Shared cross-file node: KCC2 downregulation is the convergence point across BDNF-TrkB, ana-12, GABA_apoptosis, PV+, SST, JAK-STAT, HIF1a files.

nodes.label: VEGFA (Shared Node)
nodes.rationale: Shared cross-file node: VEGFA is downstream of HIF1a, upstream of BBB disruption, linked to Ang-2 synergism, and drives BDNF/microglial activation in vegf, HIF1a, BBB, AngPt files.

links.rationale: SST.md states microglial-derived TNF-α and BDNF can enhance SST neuron excitability; BDNF also suppresses PV gate via KCC2 downregulation, indirectly releasing SST brake.
JAK-STAT.md states TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB induces IL-6 which activates JAK/STAT3; NF-kB is an upstream driver of the IL-6 autocrine loop.
NogoA-NgR1.md states Nogo-A/NgR1 signals through RhoA/ROCK which regulates MMP-9, linking myelin inhibitors to PNN degradation and PV interneuron dysfunction.
RhoA-ROCK.md states RhoA/ROCK→p38 MAPK drives microglial M1 phenotype and BDNF release; BDNF-TrkB.md confirms microglial BDNF as pronociceptive source.
hif1a.md states HIF1α induces BDNF indirectly via microglial activation; microglial HIF1α-glycolytic shift drives BDNF secretion.
IGF1-2.md notes that follistatin promotes pain by binding IGF1R; IGF1R and TrkB share downstream PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK cascades creating cross-talk opportunities.
vegf.md explicitly states VEGFA and TNF-α mutually upregulate each other, amplifying neuroinflammation.
hif1a.md states ROS inhibit PHD enzymes enabling normoxic HIF1α stabilization; GABA_apoptosis.md identifies ROS burst from mPTP opening as key calcium overload consequence.
SST.md explicitly describes disinhibition due to PV interneuron loss as the core gate-open mechanism allowing SST neurons to drive allodynia.
JAK-STAT.md states STAT3 drives BDNF expression and downregulates KCC2, both of which directly impair PV interneuron inhibitory function.
NogoA-NgR1.md links NgR1→RhoA→MMP-9→PNN degradation→PV interneuron dysfunction cascade.
Rbfox1 regulates Nav1.7 expression; SST.md states injury-induced Nav upregulation contributes to SST interneuron intrinsic hyperexcitability.
hif1a.md explicitly states HIF1α induces ANGPT2; AngPt.md details Ang-2 role in BSCB disruption and pain.
NogoA-NgR1.md states that HIF1α and vascular damage upregulate Nogo-A expression, and Nogo-A/NgR1 can influence vascular remodeling via RhoA.
hif1a.md explicitly pairs VEGFA and ANGPT2 as co-targets of HIF1α transcriptional program; microglial HIF1α-glycolysis drives the full vascular-pain axis.
Both BBB.md and vegf.md explicitly state VEGFA is a potent inducer of vascular permeability that compromises BSCB via tight junction downregulation.
Both Ang-1 and RvD1/LXA4 act as vascular stabilizers and barrier resealers via complementary mechanisms. Strategic combination could provide synergistic barrier repair.
vegf.md states VEGFA enhances NMDAR transmission and reduces inhibitory tone through BDNF-TrkB-KCC2 signaling in spinal cord.
Both IGF2BP2 (m6A reader stabilizing pain transcripts) and Rbfox1-regulated SCN9A mRNA stability operate through m6A methylation machinery on pain-relevant sodium channel transcripts.

NrCAM (Rbfox1 target) is a neuronal cell adhesion molecule; NgR1 (cell surface) interacts with LINGO-1 (also a cell adhesion molecule). Structural/functional interaction is possible but not documented.
